qa.title: UPO の意味
qa.cues: UPO / user persona / personality / internal model
qa.question: What exactly do you mean by UPO?
qa.confirm: Are you asking how we define U P O?
qa.answer: In this paper, U P O is an operational name for a response pattern associated with conversation history. We read it from the agent's responses. We do not directly measure a person's personality or the model's internal representation of a user.
qa.ja: UPO は、会話履歴に関連する応答パターンの操作的な呼び名です。応答から読み取りますが、人の性格や内部のユーザー表現を直接測ったものではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 1 と 3

qa.title: 新規性と先行研究との違い
qa.cues: contribution / novelty / new / previous work / memory architecture
qa.question: What is the main contribution compared with existing persona research?
qa.confirm: Are you asking about the contribution of the evaluation design?
qa.answer: Our contribution is an evaluation design and a comparison under controlled histories. We separate agent instructions from history, keep probes out of the main conversation, and examine meaning-related and form-related measures separately. We do not propose a new memory architecture.
qa.ja: 貢献は、履歴を制御した評価設計と比較です。指示と履歴を分け、測定用の質問を本流へ戻さず、意味に関する尺度と書き方に関する尺度を別々に見ます。新しい記憶機構を提案した研究ではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 1 と 2 および 6

qa.title: C2 と C3 で履歴は同一か
qa.cues: same history / matched / control / C2 / C3 / generated histories
qa.question: Did C2 and C3 receive exactly the same history?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether the histories were matched between C two and C three?
qa.answer: Yes. Within each matched setting, C two and C three receive the same scripted history. The added A P instructions are the difference. We are not comparing two freely generated conversations that have already developed different histories.
qa.ja: 同じ設定内では、C2 と C3 は同一の台本化された履歴を受け取ります。違いは追加の AP 指示です。自由生成の結果すでに履歴が異なる二つの会話を比較したものではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.2 と Table 1

qa.title: AP の内容と一般化できる範囲
qa.cues: AP / instructions / persona prompt / cautious / prompt design
qa.question: What instructions were included in AP?
qa.confirm: Are you asking what the A P prompt asks the agent to do?
qa.answer: The A P asks for structured, concise, and cautious responses. It also limits clarification and discourages unsupported certainty. It does not add user attributes. We tested this one instruction set, so we cannot generalize the result to every kind of agent persona.
qa.ja: 構造化・簡潔・慎重な応答、確認質問の制限、根拠のない断定の回避などを求めます。ユーザーの属性を追加するものではありません。一種類の指示セットなので、すべてのペルソナへの一般化はできません。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.2 と Table 2

qa.title: 人工的な会話を使う理由
qa.cues: synthetic / scripted / real users / realistic / natural conversation
qa.question: Why did you use scripted histories rather than real conversations?
qa.confirm: Are you asking why we used fixed synthetic histories?
qa.answer: Fixed histories let us compare the same prior conversation with and without A P. This gives us control within the experiment. However, it does not establish how an agent would behave in natural, long-term interactions with real users.
qa.ja: 同じ過去の会話を AP あり・なしで比較するためです。実験内の比較は制御しやすくなりますが、実ユーザーとの自然な長期対話で同じ結果になるとまでは言えません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.2 と 4.3 および 7

qa.title: データ数と独立な標本数
qa.cues: sample size / how many / independent / repetitions / replicates
qa.question: How many independent samples did you have?
qa.confirm: Are you asking about the number of independent lineages?
qa.answer: We had eighty lineages and four thousand three hundred and twenty responses overall. In each language, the main C two versus C three comparison used fifteen lineages per condition. Each scenario-condition cell had five repetitions. Responses within a lineage were not treated as independent samples.
qa.ja: 全体では80系列・4,320応答です。各言語の主比較では C2 と C3 が各15系列で、シナリオと条件の各セルを5回反復しています。系列内の応答を独立した標本として扱ってはいません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.1 と 4.3 および Table 1

qa.title: 測定の質問が会話を変えないか
qa.cues: probe / contamination / write back / branch / measurement
qa.question: Could the probes themselves influence later responses?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether a probe changes the later conversation?
qa.answer: Each probe is asked in a copy of the current conversation. Neither the probe nor its answer is returned to the main lineage. The main history continues separately. This prevents the probe text from becoming part of the later history.
qa.ja: 各 probe は現在の会話のコピーで実行します。質問も答えも本流へ戻さず、元の履歴は別に続きます。測定用の文章が後の履歴に混ざるのを防ぐ設計です。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.1 と 4.4

qa.title: 分離をどこまで確認したか
qa.cues: isolation / hidden state / backend / audit / leakage
qa.question: How do you know that the lineages were isolated?
qa.confirm: Are you asking what our isolation audit can verify?
qa.answer: We checked logged execution fields and reconstructed request contexts. We found no history mismatches or signs of probe write-back in that audit. However, we did not retain the raw requests sent to the provider. The audit does not prove anything about inaccessible provider-side state.
qa.ja: 実行ログと再構成したリクエスト文脈を調べ、履歴の不一致や probe の書き戻しの兆候は見つかりませんでした。ただし実際に送信した生のリクエストは残していません。アクセスできないプロバイダー内部の状態まで証明する監査ではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.3 と 4.5 および 7 と Table 6

qa.title: 埋め込み距離は妥当か
qa.cues: embedding / semantic / validity / validate / meaning
qa.question: How did you validate the embedding measure?
qa.confirm: Are you asking what the embedding measure can tell us?
qa.answer: We used text embedding three large as a proxy for differences in meaning. We checked sixteen handcrafted text pairs as a small qualitative diagnostic. This does not validate a personalization score, and the embedding distances did not cleanly separate all types of change.
qa.ja: text-embedding-3-large を使い、意味の違いを近似的に測りました。手作りの16組の文章で小さな定性的診断を行いましたが、個人化の良さを測る得点としての妥当性を示すものではなく、変化の全種類をきれいに区別できたわけでもありません。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.6

qa.title: 書き方の指標と AP が重複しないか
qa.cues: rule-based / length / overlap / confound / character count
qa.question: Do the rule features simply reflect compliance with AP?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether the rule features overlap with the A P instructions?
qa.answer: Yes, several features overlap with what A P asks the agent to do. The measure is also strongly affected by length. Removing character count changes the sign of the English contrast. We therefore treat it as a diagnostic of response form, not an independent measure of adaptation.
qa.ja: AP が要求する内容と重なる特徴があり、長さの影響も大きい指標です。文字数を外すと英語の差の符号が変わります。独立した適応の尺度ではなく、応答形式の診断として扱います。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.6 と 5.4 および 7

qa.title: 英語の信頼区間と p 値の不一致
qa.cues: significant / English / confidence interval / p-value / zero point zero five six
qa.question: Why does the English interval exclude zero when the p-value is above 0.05?
qa.confirm: Are you asking why the English interval and p-value give different threshold decisions?
qa.answer: They come from different procedures: a percentile bootstrap and a condition-label permutation test. They need not give identical threshold decisions in a small sample. We report both and describe the English evidence as weaker. We do not make a single clear-cut significance claim for English.
qa.ja: 百分位ブートストラップと条件ラベルの置換検定という異なる手続きです。小標本で二値判断が一致するとは限りません。両方を示し、英語の証拠は弱めと説明します。英語について明確な有意・非有意の一言にまとめません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.6 と 5.2 および Table 8

qa.title: 検定と多重比較
qa.cues: statistics / bootstrap / permutation / correction / multiple comparisons
qa.question: Did you correct for multiple comparisons?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether the p-values were corrected for multiple comparisons?
qa.answer: No. The p-values were descriptive and were not corrected for the family of comparisons. We used lineage-level bootstrap intervals and condition-label permutation tests. We therefore emphasize the direction, uncertainty, and consistency across measurements, rather than treating each p-value as a separate confirmed finding.
qa.ja: p 値は記述的に扱い、多重比較全体に対する補正はしていません。系列単位のブートストラップ区間と条件ラベルの置換検定を用います。各 p 値を独立した確定的発見とせず、方向、不確実性、指標間の整合性を重視します。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.6 と Table 8

qa.title: 変化が小さければ良いのか
qa.cues: better / personalization / useful / reduced drift / less responsive
qa.question: Does smaller drift mean that personalization is better?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether smaller drift is necessarily beneficial?
qa.answer: No. Smaller drift may reflect greater consistency, stronger constraints from A P, or less responsiveness to history. Our experiment cannot distinguish these explanations. We did not measure whether users preferred the responses or benefited from them.
qa.ja: 必ずしも良いとは言えません。一貫性、AP の制約、履歴への反応の弱さなどが考えられますが、区別できません。利用者が好んだか、利益を得たかも測っていません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 6 と 8

qa.title: 同じ条件でも応答がばらつく理由
qa.cues: stochastic / random / same settings / between-lineage / dispersion
qa.question: Why do independent lineages still differ under the same conditions?
qa.confirm: Are you asking about variation between repeated runs?
qa.answer: Generation is stochastic, so repeated runs can differ under the same configured settings. We measured this as between-lineage variation. A P was associated with smaller embedding dispersion in this setup, but did not remove the variation.
qa.ja: 生成には確率的なばらつきがあるため、設定が同じでも反復で応答が異なります。これを系列間のばらつきとして測りました。今回 AP は埋め込みのばらつきの小ささと関連しましたが、0にはなりませんでした。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.3 と 5.3 および Table 7

qa.title: 日本語と英語の違いの解釈
qa.cues: Japanese / English / translation / language / culture
qa.question: Can you explain the difference between Japanese and English?
qa.confirm: Are you asking how we interpret differences between the two languages?
qa.answer: The histories and probes were matched in meaning and function, rather than required to be word-for-word translations. We analyze the languages separately. This is a limited robustness check. It does not identify the cause of language differences or establish a cultural effect.
qa.ja: 履歴と probe は、逐語訳を義務にするのでなく、意味と役割を対応させました。二言語は別々に解析し、限定的な頑健性確認として扱います。言語差の原因や文化的効果を特定したわけではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.2 と 4.3 および 6 と 7

qa.title: モデルと生成設定
qa.cues: which model / GPT / temperature / tokens / generalize
qa.question: Which model and generation settings did you use?
qa.confirm: Are you asking about the model and generation settings?
qa.answer: We used G P T five point one Codex mini through the Codex command-line interface. The temperature was zero point two, with a maximum of one thousand and twenty-four tokens. We have not established that the results generalize to other models or interfaces.
qa.ja: Codex のコマンドラインから GPT-5.1 Codex mini を使い、temperature は0.2、最大トークン数は1,024でした。他モデルや別のインターフェースへ一般化することは、この研究では確認していません。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.4 と Table 4 および Section 7

qa.title: 人による評価の有無
qa.cues: human evaluation / participants / user study / ratings / preference
qa.question: Did you conduct a human evaluation or user study?
qa.confirm: Are you asking whether people evaluated the generated responses?
qa.answer: No. We did not collect human ratings in this study. The histories and probes were synthetic. Human judgments of consistency, response form, and adaptation are an important next step. The current measurements do not establish how people experience these differences.
qa.ja: この研究では人による評定は集めておらず、履歴と probe も人工的に作成しました。一貫性、応答の書き方、適応を人がどう感じるかの評価が次の課題です。現在の尺度だけでは体験上の違いは示せません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.4 と 7

qa.title: 長期記憶や別セッションへの移行
qa.cues: long-term / memory / retention / transfer / reset / persistent
qa.question: Does this show that the agent retains a user model across sessions?
qa.confirm: Are you asking about retention or transfer across sessions?
qa.answer: No. The checkpoints represent added history within the experimental setup. We did not test retention after a context reset, transfer to another model, or natural interaction over a long period. These results do not establish a persistent user model.
qa.ja: 測定時点は実験内で履歴を追加した状態です。文脈リセット後の保持、別モデルへの移行、長期間の自然な対話は検証していません。持続するユーザーモデルを示す結果ではありません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 3 と 7 と 8

qa.title: 中間時点で四つの probe を使う理由
qa.cues: four probes / core / subset / selection / intermediate checkpoints
qa.question: How did you choose the four core probes?
qa.confirm: Are you asking how the core probes were selected?
qa.answer: In a separate bilingual rerun, we ranked eligible probes by how often C three had smaller embedding drift than C two across languages and scenarios, then by the size of the differences. This favors that direction, so the intermediate checks are exploratory. The main t zero to t ten comparison uses all twelve probes and does not depend on this selection.
qa.ja: 別の二言語再実行において、指定形式・反復質問を除外し、言語×シナリオ6セルで C3−C2 が負となるセル数の多い順、正となるセル数の少ない順、平均絶対差の大きい順に順位付けしました。選択が C3＜C2 の方向を優先するため、中間時点は探索的な補助確認です。主たる t0→t10 比較は全12問を使い、この選定に依存しません。
qa.source: 論文 Section 4.4; core selection 20260319 JSON と select_dense_lightweight_probes.py

qa.title: 履歴なしの基準条件と確率的変動
qa.cues: baseline / C0 / C1 / no history / random variation / causal
qa.question: What do the no-history baselines tell you?
qa.confirm: Are you asking what C zero and C one control for?
qa.answer: C zero and C one are evaluated only before history is added. They show the initial response variation with and without A P. They are not full no-history trajectories over all checkpoints. We therefore do not claim that every measured difference is caused only by history.
qa.ja: C0 と C1 は履歴を加える前だけで評価し、AP あり・なしの初期のばらつきを示します。全時点をたどる履歴なし対照系列ではありません。測定したすべての差が履歴だけで生じたとは主張しません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.2 と 4.3 および 5.3 と Table 1

qa.title: 再現性と保存されていないデータ
qa.cues: reproducibility / raw data / payload / embeddings / seeds / logs
qa.question: What are the limitations of the reproducibility audit?
qa.confirm: Are you asking what information was not retained?
qa.answer: The logged responses support the reported analyses. However, raw request payloads and raw embedding vectors were not retained. Some provider-side settings were also not logged. We cannot claim exact reproduction of the original generation or a complete audit of hidden state.
qa.ja: 記録した応答から報告した解析を行っていますが、生のリクエストと埋め込みベクトルは保存していません。記録していないプロバイダー側の設定もあります。元の生成の完全な再現や、隠れた内部状態の完全な監査は主張できません。
qa.source: 論文 Sections 4.5 と 4.6 および 7

qa.title: 研究全体の目的と可搬性への位置づけ
qa.cues: broader goal / portability / research direction / practical implication / next step / future
qa.question: How does this study fit your broader research goal?
qa.confirm: Are you asking how this study relates to portability?
qa.answer: Our broader goal is to understand whether history-related response patterns can carry over to a new context or another model. First, we need a way to observe and compare them while examining agent instructions. This paper develops that evaluation design. It does not test persistence after a context reset, transfer to another model, or better personalization.
qa.ja: 研究全体では、履歴に関連する応答パターンが新しい文脈や別モデルへ引き継がれるかを調べたいと考えています。その前提として、エージェントへの指示を考慮しながら観測・比較する方法が必要です。本論文はその評価設計を検討する第一段階です。文脈リセット後の保持、別モデルへの移行、個人化改善は今回検証していません。

sources.title: 論文 p. 1
sources.text: Abstract Adaptive LLM-based agents can appear to adjust not only their answer content but also their response structure according to prior dialogue and user-stated preferences. This paper treats this phenomenon as a measurement problem, not as an attempt to reproduce naturalistic long-term human–agent interaction. We ask where history-conditioned user-side regularities become observable in generated responses under controlled histories. We introduce a branch-based design that separates Agent Persona (AP), the observable agent-side prior imposed by system constraints, from User Persona Observation (UPO), an operational label for responselevel user-side regularities inferred from dialogue history. Fixed probes elicit responses under inter-lineage isolation without writing probe responses back into the main lineage. Using Japanese and English tracks as a bounded bilingual robustness check, we compare an embedding-based semantic-proxy readout with a heuristic rule-based presentation diagnostic.

sources.title: 論文 p. 1
sources.text: A reconstructed-context audit checks that the AP-absent and AP-present matched-history conditions use matched injected histories and differ only in whether the AP prior is included in the observable inputs. Results show that the AP-present condition is associated with smaller embedding-space drift, with clearer evidence in Japanese and weaker but directionally consistent evidence in English. The rule-based diagnostic overlaps with AP instructions, is strongly length-sensitive, and varies by language and scenario. These findings suggest that adaptive dialogue agents should be evaluated by separating semantic-proxy drift from communicative presentation, and that UPO should be treated as an operational response-level readout rather than as a stable user trait or internal model state. In these settings, interaction quality depends not only on language capability but also on whether the system appears to adapt to a user’s explanation style, clarification needs, and task framing across turns.

sources.title: 論文 p. 1
sources.text: This concern is relevant to adaptive human–agent interaction, but this paper does not attempt to model real elapsed time, multi-session field interaction, or user change over time. Instead, it studies a narrower measurement problem for adaptive LLM-based dialogue agents: under controlled multi-turn histories, where does historyconditioned response variation become observable, and how is that variation shaped by an explicit agent-side prior? Across turns, adaptation can appear in answer content and in communicative presentation, including conclusion order, evidence, hedging, paragraphs, lists, and cautions. Because these cues may differ by language, Japanese and English serve as a bounded robustness check rather than evidence for general cross-linguistic or cultural claims. Recent work surveys persona and personalized alignment [4, 20], proposes multi-session personalization [9], and benchmarks longhorizon memory [6, 11]. These studies usually improve personalization rather than locate response-level regularity under controlled conditions.

sources.title: 論文 p. 1
sources.text: Apparent adaptation may reflect local history, system prompts, runtime policy, external memory, or latent user modeling. UPO is treated neither as a directly observable state nor as a stable human personality construct. Instead, we read it out indirectly through history-conditioned differences projected into the agent’s responses. We use the termPersona-Isolated LLMs for this experimental setting, in which the UPO readout is studied under operational inter-lineage isolation: independent conversational threads without shared cross-session memory in the logged execution context, while still allowing controlled history accumulation within each lineage. This paper addresses that measurement boundary through a controlled dialogue study that separatesinter-lineage isolationfrom within-lineage history accumulation.

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: Different lineages are operationally isolated from one another and from explicit cross-session memory, while each lineage accumulates its own injected history across checkpoints. The design also keeps evaluation probes out of the main conversational stream, thereby reducing measurement contamination. In adaptive dialogue-agent evaluation, probe prompts can contaminate later turns, and external memory layers can obscure whether apparent continuity comes from session-local history or stored cross-session state. The issue is therefore not simply whether added history changes responses, but whether history-conditioned regularity remains measurable under interlineage isolation and whether AP affects semantic and structural readouts differently under matched histories. Our design separates these targets by comparing embedding-based semantic drift with rule-based response structuring under matched histories and agent priors.

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: We contribute: (i) an operational AP/UPO formulation for adaptive LLM-based agent evaluation, (ii) a branch-based methodology for contamination-resistant controlled history measurement, and (iii) a lineage-level analysis showing that an embedding-based semantic-proxy readout and a heuristic AP-sensitive presentation diagnostic can exhibit different patterns under matched histories. 2 Related Work Prior work extracts user attributes from dialogue logs [21], detects implicit persona for personalized generation [2], and uses personaaware prompting, profiles, and reflective memory in multi-session systems [9, 18, 22]. These approaches optimize personalization quality or consistency rather than the observability of user-conditioned regularity; we therefore treat the present work as evaluation design, not a personalization-improvement method. Long-horizon dialogue work shows that consistency remains difficult [6, 11], while long-term HRI emphasizes repeated interaction, personalization, and adaptation [ 3, 8].

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: Embodied field work has also linked personalized robot service to rapport, cooperation, and engagement [7]. This is not an embodied or naturalistic long-term deployment; its methodological relevance is distinguishing whether apparent continuity comes from user-conditioned semantic alignment, AP-shaped presentation, or external memory. Accordingly, before apparent continuity is attributed to personalization, external memory, or a user model, evaluation should separate matchedhistory effects, agent-side priors, and probe-induced contamination. 3 Problem Formulation We study personalization in LLM-based interactive systems not merely as a performance optimization problem, but as a measurement boundary concerning where UPO becomes observable as a response-level readout. In this paper, UPO refers operationally to user-side regularity inferred from dialogue history, context, and explicit instructions. It is not treated as a directly measured internal variable, a persistent user model, or a measure of stable human personality or identity.

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: Instead, we estimate only its response-level readout by analyzing branch responses to fixed probe prompts after controlled history injection, rather than by directly analyzing user utterances alone. Here, within-lineage change refers to history-conditioned change in that response-level readout, whereas divergence refers to between-lineage dispersion across independently replicated lineages under matched conditions. This definition deliberately leaves construct validity bounded. A UPO readout can be partly confounded with stylistic regularization, prompt-induced formatting, or scenario-specific response conventions. Accordingly, the paper uses UPO as an operational analysis label and interprets the results as evidence about response-level history-conditioned regularities, not as evidence that the model has formed a validated or psychologically grounded representation of the user.

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: This distinction leads to the following research questions: • RQ1: Does history-conditioned change in the response-level readout of UPO appear within a lineage under inter-lineage isolation? • RQ2: Do independently replicated lineages show measurable between-lineage dispersion even under the same controlled condition? • RQ3: How strongly does the AP prior constrain the operational UPO readout of history-conditioned variation? • RQ4: Are form-level and semantic-level readouts aligned, or do they reveal different aspects of the same operational UPO readout? The paper focuses on these questions in a controlled setting. 4 Method 4.1 Method overview and operational units We propose a controlled branch-based dialogue design that operationalizes the distinction between AP and UPO under inter-lineage isolation. The design goal is to test whether history-conditioned regularity remains observable when independent conversational threads are kept separate from one another and only within-thread history accumulation is allowed.

sources.title: 論文 p. 2
sources.text: Here, isolation is defined operationally over observable execution fields rather than as a claim about inaccessible provider-side internals. Alineageis one thread under a fixed language-conditionscenario combination; acheckpoint 𝑡∈ {𝑡 0, . . . , 𝑡10} is its state after the first 𝑡 fixed history pairs; and areplicateis one independent stochastic repetition of the same setting. At each checkpoint, we copy the lineage state, append one evaluation prompt as aprobe branch, and log itsbranch responseas arecord. Probe branches are never written back, enabling within-lineage measurement without contaminating later context.

Embedding drift is lower under C3 in every scenario-language cell, whereas rule-based differences remain scenario-dependent and are largest in research-oriented histories. composite at the lineage level (JA/ALL Pearson’s 𝑟= 0.970562; EN/ALL Pearson’s𝑟= 0.999030). In Japanese, the pooled rule delta remains positive when any single component is omitted. In English, omitting character count changes the pooled rule delta from −0.194894to +0.018185, reversing its sign. Thus, the rule-based results are best treated as exploratory presentation diagnostics, with substantial length sensitivity, rather than as semantic evidence parallel to the embedding result.

sources.title: 論文 p. 7
sources.text: Together, these checks support treating the rule composite as a length-sensitive presentation diagnostic rather than as semantic evidence or strong evidence of same-lineage continuity. We read the language difference as a provisional observation rather than a settled causal claim. The observed pattern varies across scenario, language track, and measurement layer, with the largest heterogeneity in the rule-based space. Taken together, these results address the four RQs as follows. RQ1: within-lineage historyconditioned change appears under inter-lineage isolation in both languages. RQ2: independently replicated lineages still show measurable between-lineage dispersion under matched conditions. RQ3: in this setting, AP presence is associated with smaller embeddingspace drift, but not with a uniform reduction across all variation. RQ4: form-level and semantic-level readouts are not fully aligned, because the rule-based and embedding results diverge by language and scenario. 6 Discussion We summarize three observations.

sources.title: 論文 p. 7
sources.text: First, history-conditioned change remains observable within isolated lineages without explicit shared cross-session memory. Second, AP presence can be associated with smaller embedding-space drift while coinciding with larger values in the rule-based presentation diagnostic. Third, the consistent 𝐶2 >𝐶 3embedding pattern across adjacent, cumulative, checkpoint-delta, and scenario summaries supports smaller drift under AP in this setting, with clearer separation in Japanese

Smaller embedding drift is compatible with at least three interpretations: greater semantic consistency, stronger AP-induced regularization, or damped responsiveness to accumulated history. The matched-history design identifies the direction of the embeddingproxy difference but does not distinguish among these explanations or establish how users would perceive it.

sources.title: 論文 p. 8
sources.text: The rule-based diagnostic therefore qualifies the embeddingspace result rather than contradicting it: the two readouts show different AP-associated patterns rather than a single scalar amplification or suppression. Because the rule-based representation is partly sensitive to response structure, formatting, and languagespecific conventions, the Japanese-English difference should not be read as a pure difference in underlying history-conditioned variation. This distinction may matter for adaptive human-agent interaction when dialogue continuity is evaluated as a single notion of adaptation even though semantic-proxy drift and communicative presentation may change differently. The present design separates these targets by holding histories constant, manipulating AP independently, and reading out semantic versus presentation-level change with different metrics. The branch-based design also reduces measurement contamination by moving probes into side branches and keeping the main lineage untouched.

sources.title: 論文 p. 8
sources.text: The present protocol supports attribution through branch-only probes, matched histories, and separate embedding and presentation readouts; evaluation across models, AP families, and interactive human studies remains future work. 7 Limitations Several limitations remain. This study uses one provider/model, a non-interactive CLI runtime, and five stochastic replicates per scenario-condition cell; other models, interfaces, memory implementations, decoding configurations, and larger samples remain untested. The AP family is one structured-and-cautious instruction set, and lineage inference mitigates record-level pseudo-replication without increasing the number of independent stochastic replicates. Checkpoints 𝑡0–𝑡10 are injected-history states rather than observations from real-time sessions, multi-session field interactions, or user change over time. UPO is an operational response-level construct, not an observed internal state, durable memory representation, or stable personality.

sources.title: 論文 p. 8
sources.text: Histories and probes are synthetic, and no human judgments of consistency, presentation, adaptation, or personalization were collected. The reconstructed-context audit lacks raw API payload verification;top_p and provider-side seeds or stochastic states were not logged. Raw embedding vectors were not retained, so no embedding random-pair baseline was recomputed. The rule metric is heuristic, length-sensitive, and partly overlaps AP instructions. Finally, the bilingual comparison uses semantically matched parallel materials as a bounded robustness check, not a general Japanese-English or cultural claim. 8 Conclusion This paper treated personalization as a controlled measurement problem by examining where history-conditioned user-side regularity becomes observable.

sources.title: 論文 p. 8
sources.text: With the AP/UPO distinction and branchbased lineages, history-conditioned variation remained observable under inter-lineage isolation; AP presence was associated with smaller embedding-space drift, with clearer evidence in Japanese and weaker but directionally similar evidence in English, while the rule-based presentation diagnostic showed different, language- and scenario-dependent patterns. This divergence does not establish better personalization, user benefit, or a persistent user model. For adaptive human-agent interaction, continuity should be evaluated as an interaction between history-conditioned user-side regularity and the agent-side prior, rather than as a single scalar personalization variable. Future work should test this distinction in naturalistic multi-thread and embodied interaction settings. sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 1
sources.text: Thank you for the introduction. Good morning. My name is Satoshi Koda, and I'm from Tokai University. English is not my first language, so thank you for your patience. Today, I'll talk about how conversation history changes an agent's responses. We also ask how the agent's instructions affect these changes.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 2
sources.text: A short answer may reflect the user's history, or instructions to be concise. We call the added agent instructions A P. U P O refers to the history-related pattern we observe in responses. It is not a direct measurement of a user model. Our broader goal is to test whether such patterns carry over to a new context or model. This paper takes the first step by observing and comparing them under controlled conditions.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 3
sources.text: We compare four conditions. C zero has no added A P and no injected history. C one adds A P, but has no history. C two has history without A P. C three has the same history with A P. Our main comparison is C two versus C three. The A P asks for structured, concise, and cautious responses. All conditions share a common system prompt.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 4
sources.text: We call one independent run under a fixed setting a lineage. For these controlled experiments, we add fixed pairs of user and assistant messages. At each checkpoint, we copy the conversation. We ask a fixed test question, called a probe, in that copy. The probe and its answer are never added back to the main conversation. This prevents the measurement from changing the later history. Each lineage is run independently, even when the same scripted history is used. The checkpoints shown here are before any history is added, after five pairs, and after ten pairs.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 5
sources.text: We use Japanese and English, with three scenarios: research, development, and ideation. C two and C three receive ten scripted pairs of user and assistant messages. There are forty lineages per language, with five repetitions for each setting. In total, we have eighty lineages and four thousand three hundred and twenty responses. We use twelve probes at the main checkpoints, and four at intermediate checkpoints. These are synthetic histories, not conversations from real participants.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 6
sources.text: We measure responses in two ways. Embedding distance is a rough measure of differences in meaning. It is one minus the cosine similarity between response embeddings. Rule-based distance measures the form of a response, using features such as length, lists, and expressions of uncertainty. We compare answers to the same probe before any history is added and after ten pairs. We summarize the changes within each lineage. The main unit in our statistical analysis is the lineage, rather than the individual response.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 7
sources.text: Here is the main embedding result. Gray bars show C two. Teal bars show C three. So, we are comparing conditions with and without A P, using the same history. In Japanese, the mean distance is zero point two six nine without A P and zero point two three zero with A P. In English, it is zero point two six two without A P and zero point two three three with A P. The evidence is clearer in Japanese. For English, the bootstrap interval excludes zero, but the permutation p-value is about zero point zero five six. We therefore describe the English evidence as weaker. These values measure distance, not accuracy.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 8
sources.text: The rule-based distance shows a different pattern for response form. The mean distance is larger with A P in Japanese, and slightly smaller in English. However, the confidence intervals for both differences include zero, so both comparisons are uncertain. The measure is also sensitive to response length. When we remove character count, the English difference changes sign. Some features are directly encouraged by the A P instructions. We therefore use this measure to examine response form, not to judge whether personalization is better.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 9
sources.text: We can still observe variation related to history within isolated lineages. Independent runs also differ under the same conditions. A P is associated with smaller embedding drift, with clearer evidence in Japanese. Response form does not show the same pattern. Together, these results support measuring meaning-related variation and response form separately.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 10
sources.text: Does smaller drift mean better personalization? Our results do not establish that. Responses may be more consistent in meaning. The A P may constrain them more strongly. Or the agent may be less responsive to the history. Our experiment cannot distinguish between these explanations. We also did not measure user satisfaction or benefit.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 11
sources.text: Our evidence has several limitations. We tested one model and one set of A P instructions. The histories were scripted, rather than natural long-term conversations. We did not collect human ratings. Our audit checked the execution logs and reconstructed contexts, but not the raw requests sent to the provider. Using two languages provides a limited check of robustness. A next step is to test more models and include human evaluation.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 12
sources.text: We provide a controlled design with matched histories and probes used only in separate branches of the conversation. This lets us compare agent instructions without the test questions changing the later history. Our results support evaluating meaning-related variation and response form separately. This is a first step in our research on U P O portability. It does not test portability or show that personalization is better. I would be happy to hear your feedback or discuss possible applications of this framework. Please feel free to contact me. Thank you.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 13
sources.text: These are the published cumulative contrasts from t zero to t ten. The confidence intervals use the percentile bootstrap at the lineage level. The permutation tests compare condition labels, and g is Hedges' effect size. The tests are descriptive, with no correction for multiple comparisons. For English, we should report the embedding interval and the permutation p-value together. We should not reduce them to a single label of significant or not significant.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 14
sources.text: The conditions without history help show that A P changes response geometry even before history is added. At baseline, embedding dispersion is lower with A P in both languages, while rule-based dispersion is higher. When history is added, the English rule-based means are close after aggregation. But the differences at individual checkpoints change sign. So, a small pooled difference does not establish that there is no effect.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 15
sources.text: The rule-based features partly overlap with what the A P explicitly asks the agent to do. The scales are heuristic constants, fixed before the main experiment. This diagnostic measure is highly sensitive to response length. Removing individual components does not make it a validated measure of user persona. The paper also reports that the pooled rule-based differences were close to the mean values of the random-pair baseline.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 16
sources.text: The deterministic audit reconstructed request contexts from versioned prompts, probe suites, scenario histories, configuration, and row metadata. The history and non-A P layers matched across four hundred and eight templates and two thousand and forty pairs, including all repetitions. We found no signs that probes had been written back to the main conversation. This supports the observable input contrast. But it is not a byte-level audit of the actual A P I payloads. The four core probes were selected in a separate bilingual rerun. The main comparison from t zero to t ten uses the full probe suite and does not depend on that selection.

sources.title: 発表原稿 · Slide 17
sources.text: These selected studies help place our contribution in the context of evaluation design. Persona research distinguishes role-playing from personalization. Research on long-term memory tests retention over long conversations. Field studies in human-robot interaction test how personalization affects people. Our experiment focuses on a narrower comparison at the response level.
